properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's real-site pass: real, community-surveyed OpenStreetMap boundary (way 56656116), the same pattern already used for Pier 70's Crane Cove Park (data/manual/pier70_crane_cove_park.geojson) -- not a hand trace or plan-diagram estimate. HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (matches SF Rec & Park's own facility listing). OSM also carries other, smaller/overlapping ways for parts of this same park (e.g. way 579664205 further east, and way 27369705); this feature uses the single most detailed, currently-tagged way covering the park's main extent along Mission Creek's south bank. A second pass could merge the full multi-segment shoreline extent.

properties.p_number: P1 (Amphitheater, built 2002) and P3 (built) per OCII's Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update'; P2 and P8, part of the same named park in OCII's numbering, are separately listed there as unbuilt ('coming soon') and are NOT represented by this record's real, community-surveyed OSM boundary (way 56656116), which reflects only what is actually built. INFERRED which built segment maps to which of P1/P3 -- not explicitly matched in the source. (https://sfocii.org/sites/default/files/2024-11/Item%205%20-%20Remaining%20Mission%20Bay%20Open%20Space%20Parcels%20Update.pdf)
properties.notes: One of the parks completed as part of Mission Bay's original 1998 plan; open by fall 2010 per Wikipedia's Mission Bay article (citing the neighborhood's own park-completion history) and SF Rec & Park's facility page.
